doc.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

chapter: Jazz scene and learning the hard way
title: The 'Trio of Griots' storytelling project with Benny Powell and Billy Harper
summary: Students ask him for his old days stories; he, Powell and Harper plan school sessions called Trio of Griots.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: So now, I found out I wasn’t the only one, that Benny Powell the trombone player does the same thing, well he’s got quite a history too. And Billy Harper, the tenor player. So I guess the three of us were the ones who were doing it most you know, so Benny Powell proposed a project we’re going to do soon, called the Trio of Griots. I think Griot means —
Yeah. And as a group we’re going to hold sessions like that in the auditorium at school. We’re going to tell about the old days and the school is for it, they’re really high on doing it.
So we’re in the process of putting that together now. You know we’ll do it separate and we’ll do it together, for the whole school.
Sure. Well that’s why we’re doing this too.
Yeah. The same thing, right, yeah.
Right. And it won’t be long I’m sure before I’m reading some CD of some new upcoming star and they’re going to mention Junior Mance as showing me this or that. I’m sure it will happen.
